title: Analista do Associativo
description: 1. COMO É SER ANALISTA DO ASSOCIATIVO EM MSF-BRASIL? Médicos Sem Fronteiras Brasil é uma associação civil sem fins lucrativos, de caráter social e humanitário. Como toda associação, sua base é formada por pessoas que compartilham um propósito comum. Em MSF, essa comunidade reúne profissionais que atuam ou atuaram na organização, e que escolheram contribuir ativamente para a organização por meio de engajamento, pela troca de perspectivas e pelo compromisso com os princípios e valores da organização. A dimensão associativa é um dos pilares da identidade de MSF. Ela fortalece a participação de suas pessoas-membro na vida institucional da organização, promovendo espaços de diálogo, debate, reflexão crítica e construção coletiva. A área Associativa tem como objetivo fortalecer e desenvolver essa comunidade, estimulando sua participação e garantindo a boa governança institucional. Entre suas atribuições estão o apoio aos processos associativos, a organização de atividades e eventos, o fortalecimento da vida associativa e o suporte aos Conselhos Administrativo e Fiscal, contribuindo para o funcionamento democrático e sustentável da organização. 2. COMO É O DIA A DIA DA POSIÇÃO? Apoio no funcionamento geral da associação Executar as atividades do plano de ação plurianual dentro de seu escopo de maneira autônoma e regularmente informar sobre o andamento das mesmas à coordenação; Ser responsável por operacionalizar todas as etapas de organização logística da Assembleia Geral (AG) anual, e outros eventos associativos ao longo do ano, e acompanhamento de resultados em colaboração com coordenação e CA; Participar ativamente do processo de criação e desenvolvimento de ações de comunicação offline e online dos eventos associativos, desde o planejamento até o pós-produção; Ser responsável por compilar, analisar e divulgar dados e resultados referentes à Assembleia Geral para a associação MSF-Brasil; Definir, junto à Coordenação, metodologias de coleta de dados e análise de indicadores de engajamento, propondo novas ideias e melhorias para a área; Acompanhar constantemente o funcionamento da rede associativa internacional (associative network) e temas relevantes do Movimento, identificando e apontando possíveis ações de colaboração e atividades relacionadas aos objetivos estratégicos do Asso Brasil; Relação com Conselho Administrativo e Conselho Fiscal Facilitar o processo de integração e engajamento de novas pessoas, orientando-as sobre o funcionamento dos processos do Associativo de MSF-Brasil, a partir de briefings, informativos, entre outras formas; Oferecer suporte regular às pessoas do CA responsáveis pelas iniciativas associativas (Grupos de Trabalho, Comitês associativos e outros); Participar e planejar encontros periódicos e reuniões sob demanda com o Conselho Administrativo, produzindo atas e apoiando a logística conforme necessidade; Relação com pessoas associadas e executivo de MSF Brasil Propor ações para o aprimoramento contínuo e inovador na comunicação e relacionamento com as pessoas associadas, garantindo a manutenção do relacionamento com essas pessoas e membros de MSF-Brasil como um todo; Apoiar o funcionamento das iniciativas associativas no executivo, facilitando a divulgação de vagas, a integração e briefings para novas pessoas funcionárias e associadas, realizando encontros regulares, definição de agenda e o acompanhamento de tarefas prioritárias; Operacionalizar os processos do associativo, desde a adesão, atualização da base de dados, até análises e recomendações periódicas dos resultados encontrados; Gerir a caixa de e-mails e redes sociais do associativo, respondendo a demandas relacionadas aos processos da área e reportando conforme necessidade; Implementar ações de comunicação, redigindo e disparando informes regulares, a fim de manter as pessoas associadas informadas sobre as iniciativas e temas de relevância do movimento MSF; Gerir canais de comunicação do Asso Brasil, propondo melhorias de estrutura e manutenção periódica de conteúdo, contribuindo para a ampliação da visibilidade, engajamento e conhecimento acerca do Movimento Associativo em MSF-Brasil; Ser referência da Associação de MSF-Brasil para o Movimento, membros do CA, membros do executivo e pessoas associadas, junto à coordenação da área; Contribuir ativamente para um melhor fluxo de comunicação e distribuição de tarefas entre os Membros do Conselho, estrutura executiva e coordenação do Associativo, incluindo rotinas administrativas, compartilhando conhecimento e organizando reuniões; Compromissos Institucionais – MSF-Brasil Atuar de forma alinhada aos valores e princípios da organização, contribuindo para um ambiente de trabalho ético, equitativo e inclusivo, pautado pela escuta ativa, pelo respeito e pela colaboração; Conhecer e aplicar as diretrizes éticas de MSF-Brasil e os Compromissos Comportamentais da organização no exercício de suas atividades, promovendo um ambiente de trabalho respeitoso, transparente e coerente com os princípios institucionais; Colaborar com outras áreas e equipes de forma proativa, contribuindo para o fortalecimento do trabalho transversal e para a melhoria contínua de processos; Contribuir, dentro de suas atribuições, para a implementação dos objetivos definidos nos planejamentos estratégico e operacional, com responsabilidade sobre suas entregas e atenção à qualidade do trabalho; Adotar práticas que valorizem a diversidade, a equidade e a inclusão, respeitando diferentes perspectivas, combatendo qualquer forma de discriminação e contribuindo para um ambiente seguro e acolhedor para todas as pessoas; 3. O QUE VOCÊ PRECISA TER? Graduação completa; Experiência em planejamento, gerenciamento de projetos e/ou atividades administrativas; Experiência com organização de eventos e/ou projetos especiais; Nível intermediário do inglês; Conhecimento avançado de Pacote Office; Habilidades avançadas de comunicação oral e escrita; Habilidades de gestão de eventos e fornecedores; 4. O QUE AUMENTA SUAS CHANCES? Experiência em MSF e/ou com o Movimento Associativo; Conhecimentos em espanhol; Conhecimentos de governança de MSF e/ou associações; Conhecimentos em metodologia data driven; 5. QUAIS SÃO AS COMPETÊNCIAS NECESSÁRIAS? Você precisará ter orientação de serviço para compreender as necessidades de diferentes públicos, antecipar demandas e contribuir para uma experiência positiva das pessoas associadas, conselheiras e demais interlocutoras da área. Será importante também demonstrar planejamento e organização para coordenar múltiplas atividades, definir prioridades e garantir o acompanhamento eficiente de eventos, reuniões e processos associativos. Além disso, será necessário ter iniciativa e inovação para propor melhorias, identificar oportunidades e contribuir para o desenvolvimento contínuo das atividades da área, e habilidade para construir redes de contato e relacionamentos para fortalecer conexões, engajar diferentes atores do Movimento e promover a colaboração entre as diversas instâncias associativas de MSF-Brasil. PRINCÍPIOS E CULTURA DE SALVAGUARDA: MSF está em busca de pessoas que compartilhem do compromisso com uma cultura de salvaguarda, que visa garantir um ambiente seguro e acolhedor para todas as pessoas. Buscamos promover e garantir a Diversidade, Equidade e Inclusão (DEI) em todas as nossas ações e práticas. Assim, fortalecemos nossa missão e asseguramos que todas as pessoas tenham a oportunidade de contribuir e crescer na organização. Candidaturas que demonstrem alinhamento com esses valores serão altamente valorizadas. Alinhada com os valores que orientam as ações da nossa organização em todo o mundo, consideraremos apenas a candidatura de pessoas que cumpram os requisitos estabelecidos e se identifiquem como pessoas pretas, pardas ou pertencentes a comunidade indígena. title: Change Manager, LATAM OU
description: Change Manager – Role Overview The Change Manager is crucial in shaping how people experience and contribute to change across Haleon. The role enables, coordinates and executes our strategic programmes, owning the local change strategy and roadmap within an assigned Operating Unit to ensure a coherent change experience. The role focuses on the people side of change – identifying, preparing, and equipping our colleagues to adopt changes in ways of working, roles, operating models, business processes, systems, technology, culture and more. It reports into the Change Management CoE Director and supports a collaborative effort to drive change excellence at scale. Key Responsibilities Drive the execution of strategic transformation initiatives landing in assigned Operating Unit by developing a change strategy and actionable roadmap. Conduct change diagnostics (e.g., impact assessments) to identify targeted change interventions and ensure alignment to Haleon’s culture strategy during planning and execution. Support the delivery and adoption of change through facilitating workshops, defining success metrics, assessing change effectiveness, measuring adoption, and coordinating local knowledge management plans. Partner with Programmes to develop local business readiness criteria ahead of going‑live with change initiatives. Hold programme and business leads accountable for leader‑led change execution. Anticipate stakeholder needs and potential resistance, proactively identifying targeted mitigations. Coordinate change activities across stakeholders and teams (HR, Communications, Programmes, Capability Leads, L&D, etc.) and act as a bridge between programmes and local teams. Develop and oversee the implementation of local communications and engagement plans, including mapping key stakeholders, agreeing the engagement approach with business leaders and HR, and tailoring programme change narratives for local needs. Build a holistic change capability strategy and plan for assigned Operating Unit, ensuring alignment to the enterprise skills framework. Develop and execute the change learning plan and curriculum with subject matter experts, partner with Programme leads, Capability Leads, and HR to identify training needs and ensure appropriate training plans are in place, including measuring effectiveness. Coach and upskill business leaders on change management, holding them to account for role‑modeling change and culture and driving uptake in their Operating Unit. Contribute to continuous improvement and knowledge sharing through the change management community of practice. Review and report on change outcomes and benefits, grounded in metrics, with clear ROI and linked to business outcomes. Identify, document and support the mitigation of key change management risks within the assigned Operating Unit and work across workstreams to implement interventions and resolve issues. Basic Qualifications Proven track record of executing change programs within complex, matrixed environments, demonstrating effectiveness across diverse global teams. Proficiency with portfolio‑level change management, including prioritisation, sequencing and operating across interdependent transformations. Ability to translate an enterprise‑level change strategy and roadmap into an executable and measurable local adoption plan. Strong understanding of change management best practices, tools and techniques, and practical implementation. Strong communication and relationship‑building skills, simplifying complex messages for business leaders. Strong problem‑solving and planning skills, working through ambiguity and adapting delivery approaches. Ability to influence and navigate across a broad ecosystem of stakeholders, including Leaders, Line Managers, HRBPs, L&D, etc. Preferred Qualifications PROSCI and/or APMG Change Practitioner certification (preferred). Strong business acumen and understanding of business operations and operating model components. Demonstrated ability to coach sponsors, cultivate change champions and drive business accountability for change. Solid understanding of how people experience change and drivers of change, embedding mindset and culture shifts across teams. Strong data fluency, leveraging analytics and insights to drive adoption; proficiency with change management, collaboration and digital adoption tools. Our decision to hire is based solely on qualifications, experience, and fit for the role. title: Senior Solutions Architect, Media, Entertainment, Games & Sports
description: Senior Solutions Architect – Media, Entertainment, Games & Sports (MEGS) Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Senior Solutions Architect to serve as a trusted technical advisor to broadcasters, content creators, and production companies. You will help reimagine their workflows using AWS cloud technologies, working with customers across broadcast operations, live production, content creation, and media supply chain to accelerate digital transformation. The role requires approximately 10% travel, including international. Key job responsibilities Customer Engagement: Work backward from the customer to drive adoption of AWS services for media and entertainment workloads, focusing on broadcast, streaming, and content production use cases. Technical Leadership: Understand and anticipate customer business needs, accelerating their ability to innovate by building working prototypes and industry‑specific solutions. Architecture & Design: Run technical workshops and advise customers on architectural decisions for cloud‑based media solutions. Best Practices: Educate customers to ensure their solutions follow AWS best practices for scalability, availability, security, and operational excellence in media environments. Thought Leadership: Author or contribute to AWS customer‑facing publications such as whitepapers, tutorials, and blog posts focused on media technology. External Communication: Participate in industry conferences and events, sharing knowledge with the broader AWS solutions architect community and media industry. Product Feedback: Drive customer requirements alignment with AWS service teams' roadmaps, acting as the voice of media and entertainment customers. A day in the life Your days blend technical depth with strategic advisory work across broadcasters and content creators. You’ll architect cloud solutions for live sports streaming and broadcast workflows, build proof‑of‑concepts with AWS media services, collaborate with account teams on customer workshops, and share field feedback with AWS product teams. Throughout the week, you balance hands‑on customer engagements with thought leadership—mentoring junior SAs, presenting at industry conferences, and documenting architectural patterns. Basic Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience. 5+ years experience solving problems with technology in the Media & Entertainment Industry. Experience in technical solution design and customer engagement. Ability to communicate fluently in English and Portuguese in technical and business settings (verbal and written). Preferred Qualifications Experience working with and presenting to C‑level executives, IT, and lines of businesses across organizations or equivalent. Experience working with AWS Services. Experience working with or evaluating AI systems. Experience writing technical articles, speaking at technology conferences, and contributing to open source. Speak, write, and read fluently in Spanish. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit for more information. title: Brazil - Remote: Mid-Level Developer
description: About Landmark Landmark, a Halliburton company, builds the software and data platforms that help the global energy industry make better decisions. Our products span subsurface interpretation, well construction planning, reservoir simulation, production optimization, and digital operations. These are tools used daily by engineers and scientists at the world’s largest energy companies and run as cloud‑native SaaS platforms and as enterprise on‑premises solutions. About The Role You own the full development cycle for the features and systems your team assigns you. At Landmark, that means working on software that oil and gas operators depend on for high‑stakes decisions. You take a feature from specification through design, implementation, testing, and delivery with minimal supervision and enough judgment to make good technical decisions along the way. You contribute to code reviews, improve the codebase and processes around you without waiting to be asked, and help junior engineers grow. The quality of what you build shows up in production software used by operators worldwide. Strong software engineering fundamentals are the primary requirement. Domain knowledge is valuable but can develop on the job. Positions are available across a range of teams. Team assignment determines both the product domain you work in and the major technologies you use. Teams Build Software For Domains Such As Geoscience — geology, geophysics, or petrophysics Drilling engineering and well planning Reservoir engineering and modeling Production engineering and optimization E&P data management and integration Cloud and platform infrastructure, data services, and developer tooling AI-assisted analytics, search, and generative AI Technologies Used Vary By Team And Include Languages such as Java, C#, F#, C++, Python, and TypeScript Frameworks, platforms, and runtimes such as .NET, Eclipse RCP/SWT, JUnit, Angular, React, and Node.js Cloud platforms including Azure and AWS Containerization and orchestration tooling such as Docker and Kubernetes Infrastructure automation tools such as Terraform, Ansible, Helm, and Argo CD/Flux Relational and NoSQL databases such as PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, and MongoDB Job Duties Own features end to end: analyze requirements, design solutions, write the code, test it, and ship it Break complex specifications into concrete tasks with realistic schedules and flag risks early Proactively identify and fix weaknesses in the codebase, the test coverage, and the development process Investigate and resolve production defects, and trace root cause when symptom and source are not in the same place Apply secure coding practices, surface vulnerabilities in code reviews, and fix security issues as they arise Review code from other engineers with the same rigor you expect on your own work Evaluate and integrate open‑source tools and libraries where they improve the systems you work on Mentor junior engineers through code reviews, pairing, and direct technical guidance Communicate clearly across a distributed, cross‑timezone team Qualifications Required Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience 5–10 years of software development experience Strong proficiency in at least one of: Java, C#/F# (.NET), C++, Python, or TypeScript (React/Angular/Node.js) Experience owning the full development cycle: requirements analysis, design, implementation, testing, and delivery Experience debugging production software and tracing root causes that span multiple components or layers Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical decisions and trade‑offs to teammates and stakeholders Preferred Experience with cloud‑native development, full‑stack or web application development, or data platform technologies Experience with CI/CD pipelines, containerization, and infrastructure automation Background in enterprise software, SaaS platforms, or technically demanding application domains (scientific computing, real‑time systems, large‑scale data) Exposure to integrating machine learning, generative AI, or LLM‑based components into application features Experience mentoring less experienced engineers Energy industry experience is not required but is a strong plus. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and encourage you to apply even if your experience does not match every item in the preferred list. How You Work The engineer who succeeds in this role brings independent judgment to their work and applies it consistently. You own your assignments end to end, communicate clearly when something is off track, and treat code reviews as a genuine quality tool rather than a formality. You are comfortable working across time zones, adaptable when requirements shift, and focused on delivery outcomes rather than task completion. You pick up new tools and techniques on your own, evaluate them critically, and bring the ones that work to your team. You help the engineers around you improve because you understand that team quality compounds over time. Why Landmark We build small, high‑ownership teams and invest in the quality of every person on them. You will work in a business where software is the product, the work you do matters, and the standards are high. You will own real work that ships, learn from engineers who push you, and grow into the kind of engineer the team relies on. We offer competitive compensation, a strong career path, and a role where you own what you build, and your impact is visible. Halliburton is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
